requirement:
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
in `used`, as described in {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`.
rationale:
The reviewed test is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]`. It is marked {test} for the subject and covers each obligation in the subject's text.

- **First delivered result includes `instructions`, even when `matches` is empty.** `session` first runs `search_text` for `absent`, which has no matches. The test reads `empty["instructions"].as_str().unwrap()` and checks its content. A second conversation, `fresh`, runs `search_text` for `hit`, which has matches, and asserts `hits["instructions"] == instructions`.
- **Text and structural searches share the rule.** `peer` is a separate conversation whose first search is `search_structure`. It returns `matches == []` and `instructions == instructions`.
- **Failed searches leave the instructions for the first successful delivery.** `session` first dispatches `search_text` with the invalid pattern `(`, which asserts `is_err()`. The next successful search, `absent`, then carries the instructions. The test checks this only for a failed text search. It has no failed structural search, but the text states the rule once for both searches, so I did not treat that as a gap.
- **Later searches omit the field.** After its first search, `peer` runs `search_text` for `absent` and asserts `page.get("instructions").is_none()`. `session` also asserts the field is absent from its later `hit` search, which follows the closed first search.
- **Continuation pages omit the field.** `get_next_page` on `fresh` (`rest`) and on `session` (`second`) both assert `get("instructions").is_none()`.
- **Instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to put in `used`.** The test asserts the instructions contain phrases such as "Before submitting, close every delivered search page", "finish_search", "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read" and "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result". The more detailed content is covered by the refining `.content` requirement, which the same test also marks.

The test asserts each outcome, so a violation of the subject's text would be caught. I found no gaps.

text: The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
